products.name: Scoir
products.note: Verified in the research for The AI Ready School. AI: Career matching. Use: College and career planning. Who: Students grades 6 to 12, counselors, families. Student age: Middle and high school students through school accounts. Privacy: Vendor states it does not sell student personal information. Price: Free for students and families; school plans per student plus $250 setup; 50% discount per free or reduced lunch student.

profile_text.body:
Scoir describes itself as a college and career network that connects students, guardians, counselors, middle schools, high schools, and colleges. According to its site, the platform is aimed at students, families, counselors, and college admissions staff, and offers tools for college and career discovery, application support, and admissions counseling, along with an electronic document delivery system. The company says it works to expand college access and improve student outcomes.

The site presents Scoir as a privacy-first network and says it does not sell student personal information. It is free for students and families, while school plans are priced per student plus a $250 setup fee, with a 50% discount per student eligible for free or reduced lunch. The site cites one school's report that 92% of its Class of 2024 seniors applied to at least four colleges and 70% matriculated to four-year institutions, which the school attributes in part to Scoir.

Scoir's tracked product listing places it in education and research AI, with career matching as the AI function and college and career planning as its use. The listed audience is students in grades 6 to 12, counselors, and families, with student access through school accounts.
